incident-bot: ALERT: High latency SLO breach detected (p95/p99) on inference-prod-usw2. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/alerts/6789 :rotating_light:

alice: paging @oncall - seeing sustained p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.6s for text-generation API. Streaming stalls reported by a few customers.

bob: got the page, I'm looking at traces. early signs point to KV cache thrash - eviction spikes around 16:12 UTC.

carol: I see the same in the runtime dashboards — KV cache hitrate dropping from 88% -> 52% in 5m window. Prefill queue length increased.

alice: can someone post the query that surfaced this?

bob: copying logs snippet:```
[2026-02-18T16:11:52Z] service=runtime instance=gpu-23 event=kv_evict count=120
[2026-02-18T16:11:52Z] service=runtime instance=gpu-23 event=prefill_enqueue len=312
[2026-02-18T16:12:01Z] service=runtime instance=gpu-23 event=stream_stall id=abc123 duration_ms=202
```

dave: interesting — eviction spikes coincide with prefill backlog. Could be prefill vs decode imbalance: prefill filling KV, then decode accesses cause misses while eviction runs.

erin: customer impact so far? any errors or just latency?

alice: no 5xxs reported yet, mostly streaming stalls and client-side timeouts for low-latency paths. A couple of premium customers hit degraded quality-of-experience.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-022-09, severity=page, owner=@bob. Runbook: https://confluence.internal/incidents/INC-2026-022-09

bob: triage notes: region us-west2, model family: redwood-3-small-8k, load pattern: sudden multi-tenant burst from two customers at 16:05 UTC. Baseline batch sizes didn't change. KV cache total entries rose 2.4x.

carol: hypothesis: fragmentation/prefix weighting -> eviction chooses large slot entries, causing heavier decode times when those entries are refilled. Also prefill threads are saturating disk/network causing stalls.

alice: mitigation plan (short): 1) throttle prefill threads by 50% for the region; 2) bump KV eviction grace window from 30s -> 120s; 3) enable soft-fallback routing to smaller model variant for latency-sensitive customers.

bob: executing step 1 now: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/regions/usw2/prefill -d '{"concurrency_factor":0.5}'` -> OK, api returned 200.

carol: making eviction config change on runtime hosts: editing /etc/runtime/kv.conf `eviction_grace_seconds=120` and `evict_threshold=0.85` then reload. rolling reload across pool.

bob: enabling soft-fallback policy for routes tagged @premium-low-latency to use redwood-2-small while incident active. Patch applied to routing rules and staged.

alice: monitoring: p95 dropped from 420ms -> 260ms in 2 minutes after throttle + eviction change. p99 still elevated at ~900ms. Streaming stalls decreased but not gone.

dave: I've deployed a temporary adjustment to prefix scoring to prefer recently-accessed keys (LRU-ish) to reduce refills. This is a hotfix in the inference runtime. Rolling out now.

bob: hotfix in, verifying logs. I can see KV hitrate improving: 52% -> 72% over 4m.

erin: any downstream side-effects from eviction grace bump? memory pressure?

carol: memory headroom on devices was ~18% before change; with grace bumped to 120s, we hit 10% but still under safety throttle. I'll keep watching.

alice: oncall handoff note: @bob will continue as primary until 18:00 UTC, then @carol will take slack handoff if stable. Please add any ongoing tasks to the incident page.

incident-bot: NOTE: Scheduled follow-up: run focused evals for prefill/evict patterns and update Optimize recommendations. Assigned to @dave.

dave: action: run KV fragmentation scan and generate repair plan. Starting job: `tools/kv-scan --region usw2 --output /tmp/kv-scan-usw2.json`

bob: customer comms: @support, please prepare a short note for premium customers explaining transient latency and mitigations (no data loss).

alice: support: acknowledged, drafting message: "We observed transient latency between 16:05-16:25 UTC due to internal cache rebalancing; mitigation applied and normal performance resumed. We'll follow up with mitigation details."

carol: post-mitigation numbers: p95 ~210ms, p99 ~300ms. Streaming stalls near zero. KV hitrate stabilized at 81%.

erin: great. any long-term actions?

bob: long-term: 1) tune prefill concurrency heuristics (prefer prefill during low decode load), 2) rebalance KV slab allocation to reduce fragmentation, 3) add alerting for prefill queue growth + eviction spikes as correlated alert, 4) add automated fallback circuit that triggers before SLO breach.

dave: adding to backlog: implement compaction job to defragment KV store nightly and add counters for prefill vs decode bytes per second to surface skew.

alice: adding blameless postmortem task: owner @bob, due EOD +2. Please include timeline, mitigations, and follow-up PRs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: INC-2026-022-09 marked resolved at 16:40 UTC. Resolution summary: throttled prefill, raised eviction grace, enabled soft-fallbacks, applied prefix LRU scoring.

bob: closing notes: keep monitoring autoscale signals — if prefill bursts are customer-driven we may need quota changes.

carol: I'll schedule a 30m lessons-learned sync tomorrow.

erin: thanks all, nice fast coordination. :thumbsup:
